naming: Every loader builds its YamlDotNet IDeserializer with new DeserializerBuilder().WithNamingConvention(CamelCaseNamingConvention.Instance).IgnoreUnmatchedProperties().Build(). A C# PascalCase property binds to the camelCase YAML key. Dictionary keys are never renamed by the convention. Enum-like string values are parsed case-insensitively; some (like load.mode) additionally strip - and _ before matching, confirmed per-case in the file-flow census (docs/reference/flow/keys.json), not assumed for these new document kinds.

keys.description: Single-metric shorthand declaring one monitored aggregate T-SQL expression. Read from HealthCheckYaml.BaseValue and mapped by YamlHealthCheckFlowLoader.MapMetrics: when non-blank it becomes the flow's single HealthCheckMetric, whose Name is derived by HealthCheckMetric.DefaultName(expression) ('rowCount' for a bare COUNT(*), spaces and case ignored; 'value' otherwise) and whose Expression is the trimmed value verbatim. Mutually exclusive with a non-empty 'metrics' list; the exclusivity check is 'list is { Count: > 0 }', so an empty 'metrics: []' does not count as 'set', and 'baseValue' silently wins if both keys are present but 'metrics' is empty. The expression is inserted unescaped into the generated series SQL as 'CAST(<expression> AS float) AS [<name>]' (HealthCheckSqlBuilder.SeriesSelect); it is a trust boundary like preProcess/postProcess SQL (a real analogous concept: IngestionYaml.PreProcess/PostProcess and IngestionSurrogateKeyYaml.PreProcess/PostProcess elsewhere in the codebase), not a validated SQL grammar.

keys.description: Optional boolean T-SQL expression ANDed into both generated statements and shared by every metric: HealthCheckSqlBuilder.SeriesSelect appends 'AND (<filter>)' after the sentinel/as-of date bounds (only when non-blank; a blank filter emits no dangling AND), and HealthCheckSqlBuilder.DataQualitySelect ANDs the identical clause into its WHERE clause, so the same filtered row set feeds all three COUNT_BIG probes, describing the same monitored slice as the series. Also echoed verbatim into the run's HealthCheckReport.FilterCriteria artifact field. Bound from HealthCheckYaml.Filter, trimmed; inserted unescaped, the same trust boundary as baseValue and metrics[].baseValue.

Dates the calendar features treat as holidays, feeding HealthCheckEngine.ApplyDateFeatures's IsHoliday SeriesRow feature (1 when the row's calendar date is in the set, else 0). ApplyDateFeatures runs unconditionally on every run, for every metric, before HealthCheckFlowRunner.ResolveModel picks the expectation function (the ApplyDateFeatures call at HealthCheckFlowRunner.cs:258 precedes the ResolveModel call at :267), so every row's IsHoliday always reflects the flow's current holidays list, regardless of which path scores it. IsHoliday is one of the seven calendar columns the AutoML regression trains on (FeatureColumns), and it is also one of the columns the ML.NET PredictionEngine reads at Predict() time on both the fresh-train path (engine.Predict(row) at HealthCheckFlowRunner.cs:535) and the reuse path (engine.Predict(row) at HealthCheckFlowRunner.cs:400): a loaded PredictionEngine evaluates its saved transform pipeline against the row object handed to it, it does not freeze feature values from training time. So editing 'holidays' and rerunning without retraining can still change a reused stored model's scores for the affected dates, to whatever extent that model's already-fitted function is sensitive to IsHoliday; a full retrain is only what lets the model relearn the IsHoliday relationship itself. The one path genuinely blind to 'holidays' is the weekday-median baseline: BaselineModel.Predict(date) (BaselineModel.cs:45-46) keys solely on DayOfWeek and never reads IsHoliday, so a metric scored by the baseline ignores the holidays list completely. Bound from HealthCheckYaml.Holidays (a List<string>, authored as plain YAML date scalars like 2026-01-01) and mapped by YamlHealthCheckFlowLoader.MapHolidays into a deduplicated List<DateOnly>: each entry is parsed with YamlDocumentParts.ParseDate, and a date that repeats (after parsing) is silently dropped, keeping the first occurrence and preserving authored order.

keys.description: Trailing days, counted back from the run's as-of date, whose data may still be arriving. HealthCheckEngine.MarkImmaturePoints flags every row with Date >= asOfDate - (maturityDays - 1) as IsImmature. Immature rows are still scored and reported but are excluded from TagAnomalies's anomaly counting, from the observed-mature rows fed to PeltDetector.Detect for level shifts, and from ComputeMetrics's fit statistics, so a partially-loaded 'today' cannot page anyone or poison the fit numbers. 'maturityDays: 0' disables the window outright (row.IsImmature is forced false for every row: the guard is 'maturityDays > 0 && ...'), it does not merely shrink the window to zero width. Also echoed into the run's HealthCheckReport.MaturityDays artifact field.

keys.description: When the health check executes. 'auto' (the default) lets schedules and batch/node group runs pick the flow up like any other automatic execution; 'manual' excludes it from all automatic dispatch and reserves it for an explicit on-demand trigger (the GUI's run button, a single-flow API trigger, or a direct CLI run); 'disabled' deactivates it with the same exclusions and a visible 'disabled' badge. Parsed by YamlDocumentParts.ParseExecutionMode into HealthCheckFlow.Mode (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlHealthCheckFlowLoader.cs:170), backed by the ExecutionMode enum (Auto=0, Manual=1, Disabled=2).

Multi-metric form: every entry is computed in the same single scan of the target (HealthCheckSqlBuilder.SeriesSelect appends one 'CAST(<expr> AS float) AS [<name>]' column per entry to one SELECT, sharing one FROM/WHERE/GROUP BY: the 'one scan for every metric' guarantee). Mapped by YamlHealthCheckFlowLoader.MapMetrics. Mutually exclusive with the top-level 'baseValue' shorthand, but the exclusivity check only fires when this list is non-empty ('list is { Count: > 0 }'), so 'metrics: []' alongside a set 'baseValue' does not error; 'baseValue' silently wins. An absent or empty list, with 'baseValue' also blank/absent, fails to load at all.

keys.description: Container for the AutoML/detection-tuning knobs below. Bound from HealthCheckYaml.Ml; an absent block is replaced with 'new HealthCheckMlYaml()' before its six sub-keys are read ('var ml = y.Ml ?? new HealthCheckMlYaml();'), so an absent 'ml:' block behaves identically to an explicit 'ml: {}'. Unlike 'load' on the file-flow document, which maps onto a nested LoadPolicy sub-object, 'ml' has no sibling object on the immutable HealthCheckFlow model: each sub-key is validated in YamlHealthCheckFlowLoader.Map and flattened directly onto HealthCheckFlow's own top-level properties (MaxExperimentSeconds, AnomalyThreshold, EsdAlpha, MaxAnomalyFraction, Training, RetrainAfterDays).

The minimum severity, in robust (median/MAD) sigmas of prediction residual, a statistically significant ESD candidate must still reach to be tagged an anomaly: HealthCheckEngine.TagAnomalies's thresholdStdDev parameter. A flagged candidate whose Severity is below this floor is skipped outright ('anomaly.Severity < thresholdStdDev'), and the same value gates the relative-floor override at 3x: a deviation at or under the 10 percent relative floor is still suppressed unless 'Severity >= 3 * thresholdStdDev'. TagAnomalies also asserts 'ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfNegativeOrZero(thresholdStdDev)' as an internal guard, which a validly-loaded flow can never trip because the loader's own range check is at least as strict.
keys.validation: Non-finite (NaN/Infinity, e.g. authored as .nan/.inf), <= 0, or > 100 throws FlowValidationException "<source>: 'ml.anomalyThreshold' must be a positive number of standard deviations (at most 100), got <v>." keys.description: The significance level of each generalized-ESD outward test: EsdDetector.Detect's alpha parameter, used to compute Rosner's per-test critical value 'lambda_i' via a Student-t inverse CDF at 'p = 1 - alpha / (2 * nRemaining)'. Lower values require a more extreme deviation before a point is flagged. EsdDetector itself re-checks 'alpha <= 0 || alpha >= 1' and throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException "alpha must be strictly between 0 and 1." otherwise; because the loader's own range, (0, 0.5), is a strict subset of the detector's (0, 1), that internal guard can never trigger for a flow loaded through this YAML surface.
